items.topic: Update spec.json with acceptance_allow from round-001 decisions
items.context: Round-001 pre-selected targeted acceptance paths (d3), but spec.json still has no acceptance fields. These should be applied so downstream tooling (sandbox, review) can use them. Recommend option A — apply the decisions if the user agrees with them.

items.topic: Add path traversal (.. ) check to validateGlobs
items.context: validateScope already rejects '..' traversal, but validateGlobs does not. A pattern like '../secrets/**' would pass validateGlobs today. Since acceptance globs define security boundaries (acceptance_deny), this is a potential gap. However, the plan lists this as out-of-scope unless it's broken. Recommend option A — it's a one-line addition that closes a real gap.

options.label: Add .. check to validateGlobs
options.rationale: Closes a real security gap. One-line addition (strings.Contains(g, "..")). Consistent with validateScope behavior.

options.label: Skip — keep out of scope
options.rationale: The plan explicitly lists this as out of scope. Keep the fix minimal and address traversal separately if needed.

items.text: Verified: doublestar.ValidatePattern(s string) returns bool (not error). The implementation will need to construct its own error message when ValidatePattern returns false, e.g.: if !doublestar.ValidatePattern(g) { return fmt.Errorf("glob[%d]: invalid pattern %q", i, g) }. This is a minor adaptation from the current filepath.Match error-based approach.

Existing types_test.go already tests api/** as valid (line 37), which currently passes because filepath.Match silently accepts ** without error. After switching to doublestar.ValidatePattern, this test will continue to pass — but now the validation is semantically correct. No test changes needed for existing cases; only additions for better coverage.

plan_updates: No plan.md changes needed — plan is complete from round-001. Round-002 addresses spec.json metadata gaps and a potential traversal check addition.
